transcript.text:
When a dishwasher 'won't come on' at all—meaning no lights, no display, and no sound—it usually points to a lack of power reaching the control panel. The most common causes are simply that the plug has worked loose or a circuit breaker in your consumer unit has tripped. Please check two things:
1. Is the plug firmly inserted into the wall socket?
2. Has the fuse for that circuit tripped (look at your consumer unit)? If you find it's plugged in and the power is on, but there is still no sign of life, let me know if you see any faint flickering lights or hear a click when you press start.
its integrated so no plug visible, theres a switch above the worktop and its on with the light lit. nothing tripped in the consumer unit. no lights or clicks at all

Since the switch above the worktop is lit but the dishwasher remains completely dead, it’s possible the switched spur socket itself has failed internally or lost connection. Please test that socket by plugging in a small lamp or phone charger to see if it works. If the socket has no power, you’ll need an electrician to fix the spur. If the socket is working fine, we then know the fault is inside the dishwasher (likely the mains input module or control board). To help me identify the right parts if needed, could you also provide the make and model number of the dishwasher? This is usually found on a sticker on the side edge of the door.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
its a Neff, model on the door edge label is S513G60X0G. the spur is a switch above the worktop, not a socket, so I can't plug anything into it. other sockets and lights work fine though

Since the switch above your worktop is most likely on, the consumer unit hasn't tripped, and other appliances in that area are working fine, we can rule out a general power failure. The issue is probably inside the dishwasher itself—likely the mains input module or the control board has failed. Because this involves opening the appliance casing to access internal electrical components, it is not safe for you to attempt further repairs yourself. You will need to call an engineer to diagnose and replace the faulty part.

candidates: Power supply issue (trip or loose plug) (high)
Control panel lockout or timer knob position (medium)
plan: The fault they reported is: "won't come on". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the one or two safe checks, or the one question, that would best tell those causes apart. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
